questions.question: How should supervisor-restart.sh make forks visible in the desktop app?

options.label: Probe `claude --remote-control --resume <uuid>` first
options.description: Test on one fork: if it spawns a `cse_` AND keeps the transcript, use it as the default trigger (each fork becomes a connected `cse_` like any other remote-control session, shows in unified list, supervisor adopts it). If it doesn't work, fall back.

options.label: Spawn `claude remote-control --name resumed-<short>` per fork
options.description: Definitely works — mints a fresh cse_ and the supervisor adopts it. But the new cse_ has its own empty transcript; you'd have to `-r` separately in that session. Probably wrong shape.

options.label: Open Claude.app to cwd and rely on /resume picker
options.description: Script just runs `open -a Claude.app ~/dev/ai-harness` after forking. User picks the fork from /resume. No automation past surfacing the app.

I'd default the script to **NOT** auto-open (just print the resume commands) and offer `--open-terminal` for those who want the terminal flow.
